home.title: Visible structure. Independent logic.
home.tagline: RX expresses structure. ZX defines atomic logic.
home.description: zxc is a programming language and compiler designed for AI collaboration. Connect small, independent units through explicit data flow, then compose them at every scale with the same rules. Let the business grow while its structure stays clear, traceable, and maintainable.
home.rxDescription: RX uses XML for business structure: tags identify steps, nesting shows hierarchy, and attributes make call targets and data connections explicit. Visible boundaries help people and AI read, generate, and check the structure, using the same composition rules as the business grows.
home.zxDescription: ZX uses TypeScript-like syntax so familiar functions, objects, type annotations, and expressions can carry atomic logic, reducing the cost of reading and writing a new language for people and AI. A limited grammar with explicit types and ownership supports static checks and compiler optimization.
home.howDescription: ZX passes parsing, type and ownership checks, becomes typed IR, and generates Zig. RX structure validation checks module structure and dependencies. Together these establish a foundation for traceable business composition and optimizable local computation.
home.hostDescription: Today, a host executes the generated Zig and supplies memory, I/O, and state commits. Business composition, atomic computation, and external capabilities each have a clear responsibility boundary.
home.aboutDescription: zxc is an experimental project by MATRIXAGES. ZX compiles to Zig; RX validates structure and dependencies. The full RX runtime is still ahead. Feedback and concrete examples are welcome.
home.whyDescription: When workflows, computation, and state intertwine, a local change can ripple through the whole system. People and AI must first reconstruct the relationships before deciding what to change. More code makes that understanding more expensive.
home.whyApproach: zxc gives business structure to RX and atomic logic to ZX. Boundaries and connections make it explicit where data comes from, which computations it passes through, and where it goes. Compiler dependency checks keep structural constraints in place as the business grows.
home.useIntro: A ZX unit handles one computation with a clear boundary. RX composes units into business modules, and modules into larger business boundaries. When more detail is needed, split the internals again. Each level keeps a single responsibility, explicit inputs and outputs, and one-way dependencies: the fractal organization of zxc.
home.agentDescription: Built-in dependency analysis makes file, call, and type relationships checkable facts. We want to expose this graph directly to AI: locate relevant units, trace upstream and downstream relationships, assess change impact, and retrieve context on demand, with a trail for every change.
home.agentContext: The goal is to minimize token use and cognitive load, helping non-SOTA models meet the same code quality standards as SOTA models through explicit contracts and compiler feedback.
home.returnDescription: Should free shipping use the original subtotal or the discounted amount? That rule belongs in the quote unit. Changing it leaves the RX cart and order connections intact; follow dependencies to confirm callers accept the new shipping result.
home.returnReview: Atomic logic does not mean a file for every line. Split by independent business responsibility and contract. Stable boundaries help contain changes as the application grows; extra files alone do not remove coupling.
home.judgementDescription: A compiler can check a type. Whether a discount is fair—or a rule keeps your promise to a customer—needs business judgment.
home.principle: Build with atomic logic. Grow through fractal structure.
home.boundaryZx: Atomic computation, type and ownership checks, and Zig generation.
home.boundaryRx: Business structure, module boundaries, and dependency validation.
home.boundaryYouDetail: The rule itself, the examples, and the decision to ship.
home.changeCaption: The same data contract. A different pricing rule.
home.changeNote: Quote function excerpt: the free-shipping condition moves from subtotal to discounted amount.
home.flowLabel: From atomic logic to fractal business structure
home.performanceDescription: A ZX unit has a clear boundary for analysis and optimization, like a computational operator.
home.performanceFuture: Formal proofs · assembly-level optimization and generation · FPGA targets. These directions require dedicated proof tools and synthesis backends.
home.judgementCompiler: Checks types, ownership, and language constraints.
home.judgementAgent: Writes changes within explicit module boundaries.
home.judgementYou: Provide meaningful examples, decide the expected behavior, and review the result.
home.performanceInlining: Inlining — expose small computations to the optimizer.
home.performanceSpecialization: Specialization — use known types and inputs to simplify code.
home.performanceOverhead: Less overhead — aim to resolve abstractions at compile time.
home.performancePath: ZX compiles to Zig; Zig’s LLVM backend provides further optimization and machine-code generation.

copy.prompt: Use zxc for this task. Read {url} first. Confirm the available compiler and host runtime capabilities. Separate RX orchestration from ZX logic, keep dependencies acyclic, and report only checks you actually ran. Ask for the business goal and expected inputs and outputs if they are missing.
